module: Third-party library: Mike Pall's LuaJIT profiler (jit.p), copyright 2005-2016, MIT license. It is a simple interface to the low-overhead profiler built into LuaJIT (jit.profile module). It samples the call stack at regular intervals and prints a summary (functions, module lines, VM states, zones) to a file or to standard output. A modder can use it in the vehicle VM to find the most expensive Lua functions.
usage:
extensions.load('profiling_p')
profiling_p.start('vl', 'profil.txt') -- modes: see notes
-- ... let it run ...
profiling_p.stop(true)
notes: start mode string (combinable): f = stack with function names (default); F = same with module; l = module:line; <number> = stack depth; -<number> = inverted depth; s = split after the first level; p = full paths; v = VM states; z = zones; r = raw counts; a / A = annotate excerpts / full source files; G = raw output for graphical tools (flame graphs); m<number> = minimum percentage displayed (default 3); i<number> = sampling interval in ms (default 10).
If outfile is nil, the LUAJIT_PROFILEFILE environment variable is used; otherwise standard output. The value '-' forces standard output.
stop(false) stops sampling without writing a result. A garbage collection of the internal object (prof_ud) also calls prof_finish.
Mode z loads require('jit.zone'); in this folder the zone library is the neighboring file zone.lua, which is not necessarily loadable under that name (inferred from code).

start.desc: Starts profiling with the given mode and chooses the output destination (file opened for writing, or standard output).

outfile.desc: output file, '-' for standard output; nil = LUAJIT_PROFILEFILE or standard output

stop.desc: Stops the profiler and, if doOutput is true, writes the result (display of the top entries or source annotation). Writes "[No samples collected]" if no sample was taken.
